text.title: Retro Facilitation Multistyle: Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when facilitating retros across the five supported formats in real teams. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Live format on an async team: mad-sad-glad or lean-coffee run in the one overlap hour; the outsourced timezone contributes nothing and the action list reflects one office.
failure-mode.detector: `team_state.distribution == async` with any format other than `anonymous-async`; card or attendance count from one timezone under half of the others.
failure-mode.repair: Switch to `anonymous-async` with a collection window spanning every timezone (`r-format-matches-distribution`, `r-anonymous-async-window-and-clustering`).

failure-mode.description: Same format forever: the team has run the same three columns for a year; the third column is empty and the same three complaints recur.
failure-mode.detector: Identical `format` in three or more consecutive instances; `fatigue_signal` fatigued or rotating with no format change; card count declining across instances.
failure-mode.repair: Rotate to a format not used in the last two retros and cite the previous formats in the rationale (`r-fatigued-team-rotates-format`, `r-rationale-names-distribution-fatigue-and-history`).

failure-mode.description: Action avalanche: the retro ends with eight action items owned by "the team", none with a ticket; at the next retro none are done and nobody remembers them.
failure-mode.detector: More than 3 `action_items`; any `owner` that is not a single named person; missing `evidence_link` or `due_date` later than the next retro.
failure-mode.repair: Cut to 1-3 items, each with a named owner, a tracker link created during the retro and a due date before the next one; demote the rest to notes (`r-action-items-one-to-three-owned-dated-linked`).

failure-mode.description: No memory: new cards are collected before the previous actions are reviewed; the same blocker is raised for the fourth retro running and `outcome_review.last_run_at` is months old.
failure-mode.detector: Previous instance's `action_items` have no recorded done / not-done / dropped status; `outcome_review.last_run_at` earlier than the previous `retro_date`; recurring card text across instances.
failure-mode.repair: Open every retro with the status walk of the previous actions, carry over at most once, drop with a reason on the second miss (`r-previous-actions-reviewed-before-new-ones`).

failure-mode.description: Status meeting in disguise: the line manager sits in, no safety check is run, and the retro is a round of "all fine" with one person reporting.
failure-mode.detector: No Prime Directive and no safety-check result recorded in the instance; a non-member manager present in the discussion; safety median below 3 with no switch to anonymous input.
failure-mode.repair: Read the Prime Directive, run the anonymous 1-5 safety check, switch to anonymous cards when the median is below 3, and keep non-member managers out of the discussion (`r-prime-directive-and-safety-check`).

failure-mode.description: Timebox blowout: a two-week sprint retro runs two and a half hours, the first lean-coffee topic eats forty minutes, and the team votes with their feet next time.
failure-mode.detector: No timebox recorded before the retro; actual duration over the published timebox; a lean-coffee topic extended more than twice or run without a dot-vote.
failure-mode.repair: Publish the timebox in the instance (at most 3 hours for a one-month iteration, proportionally less), dot-vote lean-coffee topics, cap extensions at two, and feed overruns into the next fatigue signal (`r-timebox-published-and-held`).
